atmosphere.label: Earth atmosphere
atmosphere.text: Earth has a substantial atmosphere and a water cycle. Local conditions vary with place and time.

weather.label: Dated Earth records
weather.text: NASA POWER provides historical daily meteorological model/reanalysis values. NASA EONET supplies dated natural-event catalogue entries. These products do not establish current conditions at every selected point.

water.label: Local water not classified
water.text: Earth has oceans, surface water and ice. This layer does not yet retrieve a spatial land/water or ice mask. Daily precipitation is not a measurement of standing water.

temperature.label: 2025 daily meteorological context
temperature.text: Skin temperature and 2 m air temperature are separate physical variables. The original POWER native meteorological grid is approximately 0.5° latitude by 0.625° longitude.

atmosphere.label: Thin, mostly carbon-dioxide atmosphere
atmosphere.text: Mars has a thin atmosphere, largely carbon dioxide. Its surface pressure and wind cannot be replaced with Earth weather values.

weather.label: Current storm status unavailable
weather.text: Mars experiences winds, seasons and dust storms. This application has no current global Martian storm feed; Earth EONET markers do not apply to Mars.

water.label: Water-ice evidence; no local water map
water.text: NASA describes water ice in the polar regions and beneath the surface. This reference does not establish ice or liquid water at the selected terrain footprint.

temperature.label: Historical MEDA ground-temperature record
temperature.text: The separate temperature module uses a dated, local Perseverance MEDA record. It is not a current global temperature map or an air-temperature measurement.

sources.title: NASA PDS Mars 2020 MEDA calibrated environmental data, sol 29

atmosphere.label: Extremely thin exosphere
atmosphere.text: The Moon has an extremely thin exosphere rather than an Earth-like atmosphere.

weather.label: No Earth-style wind or rainstorms
weather.text: The lunar exosphere is too thin to produce Earth-style wind, rain or snowstorms. Space weather is a separate phenomenon and is not monitored by this layer.

water.label: Polar water-ice evidence
water.text: NASA reports evidence of water ice in permanently shadowed polar regions. This reference does not verify ice abundance, accessibility or presence at an arbitrary selected coordinate.

temperature.label: Diviner product; no live weather
temperature.text: The separate lunar thermal comparison uses a dated Diviner-derived product with its own spatial resolution and physical definition. It is not an instantaneous thermometer reading.
